sampling_model.design: The optimization input is \((G,K,\Sigma,N_{\exp})\), and the output is a labeled nonempty \(G\)-connected \(K\)-partition minimizing \(V\).
sampling_model.treatment: No assignment law is imposed by the optimization theorems; the coefficient \(2^{m+1}\mathbf 1\{m>0\}\) is frozen as part of the algebraic input criterion.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed by the optimization theorems.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The rational pilot matrix \(\widehat\Sigma\) is fixed before optimization, and the deterministic regret theorem compares it with \(\Sigma\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Appendix B.1 proves Theorem 1's residual decomposition, while Section 3.2 explains and justifies omitting its second-order residual-covariance term from the graph-cut optimization.
Their dynamic program constructs connected parts of prescribed sizes on bounded-treewidth graphs.
Their rank-based method compresses partition states for standard weighted connectivity problems.
Their worst-case cluster design is a penalized min-cut computed through semidefinite optimization.
Their pilot-based network design has oracle-regret guarantees for another variance criterion.
Their robust design optimizes over assignment covariance matrices by SDP and randomized rounding.
Their spatial cluster construction is rate-optimal under decaying interference and supports asymptotic inference.

body.tldr: Appendix B.1 of Zhu et al. supplies the imported \(p=1/2\) residual-covariance multiplier \(2^{m+1}\mathbf 1\{m>0\}\); thereafter \(V\) is an algebraic symmetric-rational optimization input. The project supplies an exact general MILP and a sound-complete fixed-parameter dynamic program on the covariance-scope interaction graph, with completed-label connectivity states, once-only scope charges, an exact rational optimum, and a checkable backpointer certificate. A four-cycle shows that the Section 3.2 surrogate can reverse the exact ordering even with entrywise-nonnegative \(\Sigma\), and ordered-entry pilot error yields an explicit criterion-regret bound.

project_justification.gap: Appendix B.1 of Zhu et al. proves Theorem 1, whereas Section 3.2 explains and justifies omitting its second-order residual-covariance term from graph-cut optimization; generic connected-partition algorithms do not supply the scope localization, closure invariant, exact rational arithmetic, or reconstruction certificate needed to optimize the imported \(p=1/2\) criterion.
project_justification.niche: For a symmetric rational objective of the form \(V\), covariance support can induce an interaction graph of moderate treewidth even though connected design remains globally coupled.
project_justification.fill: The MILP covers every finite rational instance without covariance-shape restrictions, and the sound-complete treewidth algorithm certifies and reconstructs the exact optimum; the reversal witness and perturbation theorem establish why exactness matters and how pilot error propagates.

body.related_work: Appendix B.1 of Zhu et al. proves their Theorem 1 residual decomposition; under its repeated-outcome residual setup, the fair-coin specialization supplies the factor \(2^{m_{ii'}(\mathcal C)+1}\mathbf 1\{m_{ii'}(\mathcal C)>0\}\) and hence the residual-covariance expression \(N_{\exp}^{-1}\sum_{i,i'\in U}2^{m_{ii'}(\mathcal C)+1}\Sigma_{ii'}\mathbf 1\{m_{ii'}(\mathcal C)>0\}=V(\mathcal C;\Sigma)\). That calculation is imported background rather than a theorem target. Section 3.2 explains and justifies omitting the associated second-order term from the graph-cut objective. Zhu et al.'s Assumption 2 is covariance decay, not entrywise nonnegativity; entrywise nonnegativity is an additional regime used in Proposition 2 and in the four-cycle witness here, but neither exact optimization theorem requires it. Casel, Giannopoulou, and Niklanovits provide the closest connected-partition dynamic program, whose forget and join logic informs the active-component invariant but whose objective and counters differ. Bodlaender, Cygan, Kratsch, and Nederlof supply the partition-state language and the possible representative-set strengthening. Viviano and coauthors optimize a worst-case penalized cut criterion rather than the pilot-specific scope risk. Thiyageswaran and coauthors optimize a robust assignment-covariance criterion by semidefinite relaxation and rounding, not an exact connected partition. Viviano's two-wave design supplies the adjacent pilot-to-oracle regret template. Leung supplies the spatial cluster-randomization inference benchmark after a design is chosen. Holtz and coauthors document the interference-bias and power cost in Airbnb pricing experiments that makes an auditable covariance-aware clustering decision operationally relevant.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The parameter is the treewidth of \(F\), not of \(G\). Dense pilot covariance makes every relevant exposure-scope union a clique and can force \(w\) to be of order \(R\), leaving the MILP as the exact fallback and removing practical fixed-parameter advantage.
body.honest_scope: The \(p=1/2\) multiplier is imported from Zhu et al.'s Appendix B.1 and is not a theorem contribution. The MILP exactness, dynamic-program soundness and completeness induction, reconstruction certificate, and perturbation bounds concern the already-defined rational objective \(V\) and require no potential-outcome model, assignment law, positive semidefiniteness, entrywise nonnegativity, or positive trace. The four-cycle separation additionally verifies positive definiteness and entrywise nonnegativity, placing the reversal inside the optional regime used in Zhu et al.'s Proposition 2. The delicate unresolved step is the join and forget induction for labels that disappear from a separator. Replacing every exposure neighborhood by the singleton \(\{i\}\) reduces the criterion to \(4N_{\exp}^{-1}\sum_k\sum_{i,i'\in C_k}\Sigma_{ii'}\), the spatial-correlation expression in Zhu et al.; for \(K=1\) it reduces to their global residual value. Rank-based single-exponential compression remains the open-ended question.
